MintyRobot Terms of Service

Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 December 2026
Applies to: MintyRobot contracts concluded on or after the effective date
Language versions: Slovak and English (this one). In case of conflict, the version in the language in which the contract was concluded prevails.

In short (non-binding summary): We build your website with the help of artificial intelligence and people, host it, back it up and make changes to it according to your plan. You pay monthly or yearly through our payment partner Lemon Squeezy. Your subscription renews automatically and you can cancel it at any time in the app; your website stays online until the end of the paid period. We refund your first payment in full within 14 days. Your texts, photos, logo and domain remain yours. The full text below is binding.

1. Introduction and definitions

1.1 These terms of service (the "Terms") govern the rights and obligations between the Provider and the Client in connection with the MintyRobot service.

1.2 Definitions:

  • Provider – Netova pomoc s. r. o. (details in Section 2).
  • Client – a natural or legal person who orders the Service or starts the Trial. A Client is either a Consumer (a natural person acting outside their trade, business, craft or profession) or a Business (all other Clients, including sole traders ordering a website for their business).
  • Service or MintyRobot – a subscription "website as a service": creation of a website, its operation (hosting), security, backups, updates, edits and traffic measurement within the selected Plan.
  • Plan – the scope of the Service: Start, Business or Business+ (Section 4).
  • Website – the Client's website created and operated as part of the Service.
  • Client Content – texts, photographs, logo, data, questionnaire answers, recordings and other materials supplied by the Client or created on the Client's instruction while using the Service.
  • App – the MintyRobot customer application (web version, iOS and Android) through which the Client manages the Service.
  • Edit – a request to change the Website as defined in Section 11.
  • Lemon Squeezy – the merchant that sells the Service subscription as Merchant of Record (Section 3).
  • Trial – the free 7-day trial of the Service (Section 5).

1.3 If the Client is a Consumer, nothing in these Terms limits the rights granted by mandatory consumer protection law, in particular Slovak Act No. 108/2024 Coll. on Consumer Protection, the Slovak Civil Code and the law of the country where the Consumer has their habitual residence (Section 24).

1.4 If the Client is a Business, the relationship is governed by the Slovak Commercial Code; provisions expressly intended for Consumers do not apply to Businesses unless stated otherwise.

2. Provider and contact details

2.1 Provider: Netova pomoc s. r. o., registered office at Karpatské námestie 7770/10A, 831 06 Bratislava – Rača, Slovak Republic, company ID (IČO): 54 630 649, tax ID (DIČ): 2121741941, VAT ID: SK2121741941, registered in the Commercial Register of the Municipal Court Bratislava III, Section Sro, Insert No. 161114/B.

2.2 Contact for exercising your rights (withdrawal, complaints, requests for redress):

  • e-mail: nikol@netovapomoc.sk
  • phone: +421 950 244 327
  • in the App: Account → Help
  • office: Sky Park Offices, Bottova 2A, Bratislava, Slovakia

2.3 Supervisory authority: Slovak Trade Inspection (Slovenská obchodná inšpekcia), Inspectorate for the Bratislava Region (www.soi.sk). Data protection supervision: Office for Personal Data Protection of the Slovak Republic.

3. Sales through Lemon Squeezy (Merchant of Record)

3.1 The Service subscription is sold and payments are processed by Lemon Squeezy (Lemon Squeezy LLC, or the Stripe group entity shown at checkout and on the receipt). Lemon Squeezy acts as Merchant of Record, i.e. as an authorised reseller that collects payment from the Client, issues the receipt/invoice and accounts for VAT or other sales tax according to the Client's country.

3.2 When paying, the Client also accepts the Lemon Squeezy Buyer Terms, which govern the payment transaction itself. These Terms govern the content, scope and quality of the Service provided by the Provider.

3.3 The Provider is responsible for the Service. The Provider is liable to the Client for any lack of conformity of the Service, for its proper provision and for handling withdrawals and complaints. Where the Client is entitled to a refund under these Terms or by law, the Provider will arrange the refund through Lemon Squeezy; if Lemon Squeezy does not make it for any reason, the Provider will refund the Client directly within the statutory time limit.

3.4 If the Lemon Squeezy Buyer Terms and these Terms differ on the Client's rights against the Provider (in particular refunds, withdrawal, cancellation), the provision more favourable to the Client applies.

3.5 The subscription cannot be purchased in the mobile App downloaded from the App Store or Google Play. It is purchased in the web version of the App or on the Provider's website.

4. Description of the Service and Plans

4.1 Every Plan includes:

  • design and creation of the Website based on the Client's questionnaire and materials (Section 12),
  • operation of the Website on the Provider's infrastructure (hosting), SSL certificate, security and software updates,
  • daily backups of the Website,
  • uptime monitoring and basic traffic measurement (Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console) shown in the App,
  • connection of the Client's own domain,
  • monthly Edits within the Plan (Section 11),
  • access to the App.

4.2 Plans (prices excluding VAT):

Plan Monthly Yearly Edits per month In addition to the lower plan
Start €7.90 €79 (first year €59) 3 website with up to 5 subpages
Business €17.90 €179 10 domain and 3 business mailboxes included, keyword-based SEO, Google Business Profile, forms, monthly traffic report
Business+ €35.90 €359 minor edits under fair use (Section 11.5) online bookings, review collection, 1 additional language version

4.3 The current scope of each Plan is shown in the App and on the sales page when ordering. The scope valid at the time the contract was concluded or last renewed applies (changes under Sections 15.5 and 23).

4.4 Add-ons (e.g. logo design €30 excl. VAT, additional AI visuals with people €9.90 excl. VAT each beyond the 2 included, Edits beyond the limit, additional mailboxes or languages) are provided only if expressly ordered by the Client at a price communicated in advance.

4.5 Unless agreed otherwise, the Service does not include: an online shop, custom programming, integrations with third-party systems, copywriting beyond the questionnaire, legal services (e.g. drafting terms or privacy policies for the Client's website), management of ad campaigns or any guarantee of search engine rankings.

5. Trial

5.1 The Client may start a free 7-day Trial in the App without entering payment details. The Trial may be used once per Client or business.

5.2 During the Trial the Provider prepares a preview of the Website on a trial address. The preview may contain a watermark, is not intended to be indexed by search engines, and the Client may submit up to 3 Edits. The Website is published on the Client's domain only after the subscription is paid.

5.3 The Trial ends automatically after 7 days and nothing is charged. We remind the Client one day before the Trial ends.

5.4 If the Client does not start a subscription, the Website preview is switched off. We keep the Client Content and the preview for another 30 days in case the Client decides later, and then delete them (details in the App Privacy Notice).

6. Conclusion of the contract

6.1 The Service contract is concluded when the subscription is paid at the Lemon Squeezy checkout opened from the App or the sales page. Before submitting the order, the Client is shown the Plan, the period, the total price including VAT for their country, information about automatic renewal and how to cancel.

6.2 Before paying, the Client confirms in the App that they have read these Terms and the Privacy Notice. A Consumer additionally expressly requests that performance of the Service begins before the withdrawal period expires and acknowledges the information in Section 8.

6.3 After the contract is concluded, the Provider sends the Client an e-mail confirmation containing these Terms (PDF), the withdrawal information and confirmation of the request under Section 6.2. The Client can download the Terms in the App at any time.

6.4 The contract is concluded for an indefinite period with a subscription period of one month or one year, which renews automatically (Section 7).

6.5 The Client must provide accurate details and state whether they order as a Consumer or a Business (a Business with a VAT ID enters it at the Lemon Squeezy checkout).

7. Prices, payments and automatic renewal

7.1 Prices in the App and on the sales page are shown excluding VAT. Lemon Squeezy adds VAT or other tax according to the Client's country and shows the total price before payment. A Consumer always pays the total price shown before submitting the order.

7.2 The subscription is paid in advance for the whole period (monthly or yearly) using the payment method entered at the Lemon Squeezy checkout.

7.3 Automatic renewal. At the end of each period the subscription renews automatically for the same period at the renewal price and the payment is charged to the stored payment method until the Client cancels (Section 9). For yearly subscriptions we send a reminder at least 7 days before renewal.

7.4 Introductory price. The price of €59 excl. VAT for the Start Plan applies only to the first yearly period. From the first renewal the regular price of €79 excl. VAT per year applies. This is shown when ordering.

7.5 Changing Plans. An upgrade takes effect immediately; the Client pays the pro-rated difference until the end of the current period. A downgrade takes effect from the next period. Some features may end on downgrade (e.g. language version, bookings, included mailboxes); the Provider will tell the Client in advance what changes and let them download the affected Client Content.

7.6 Price changes. The price does not change during a paid period. The Provider may change the price for future periods for the reasons in Section 23.2; it will notify the Client by e-mail and in the App at least 30 days before renewal. If the Client disagrees, they can cancel before renewal at no charge; the new price applies only after renewal.

7.7 Receipts are issued by Lemon Squeezy. The Client finds invoices and payment card management in the App (Account → Manage subscription), which redirects to the Lemon Squeezy customer portal.

8. Right of withdrawal and 14-day money-back guarantee

8.1 Money-back guarantee for all Clients

If, within 14 days of the first subscription payment, the Client notifies us that they withdraw from the contract or cancel the subscription, the Provider will refund the entire first payment, whether the Client is a Consumer or a Business and whether a monthly or yearly period was chosen. The guarantee applies to a Client's first payment for the Service (not to renewals, upgrade top-ups, or separately ordered add-ons already delivered). The refund terminates the contract and the Website is switched off.

8.2 Statutory right of withdrawal for Consumers

a) A Consumer may withdraw from a distance contract without giving any reason within 14 days of the day the contract was concluded (Sections 19 and 20(1)(a) of Slovak Act No. 108/2024 Coll.; Article 9 of Directive 2011/83/EU).

b) The Service starts immediately after payment. When ordering, the Consumer expressly requests that performance begins before the withdrawal period expires and acknowledges having been informed that:

  • if the Service is fully performed within the period, the right of withdrawal is lost; a subscription Service is normally not fully performed within the period, so the right of withdrawal lasts the full 14 days;
  • if they withdraw after performance has begun, the law entitles the trader to payment for the service actually provided up to the withdrawal (Section 21(5) of Act No. 108/2024 Coll.; Article 14(3) of Directive 2011/83/EU).

c) The Provider waives that entitlement: on withdrawal from the first payment, it will refund the Consumer in full under Section 8.1 and will not claim a proportionate amount.

d) How to withdraw:

  • in the App using the "Withdraw from contract here" function (Account → Subscription), where the Consumer enters or confirms their name, contract details and e-mail and confirms by pressing "Confirm withdrawal"; we will promptly send an e-mail confirmation with the date and time of submission; or
  • by any clear statement sent to the e-mail or address in Section 2, or using the model form in Annex 1.

e) The deadline is met if the Consumer sends the notice no later than the last day of the period.

f) The Provider will refund all payments within 14 days of receiving the withdrawal, using the same payment method (via Lemon Squeezy), free of charge.

g) After withdrawal the Provider switches off the Website and, on request, makes the Client Content available free of charge in a commonly used, machine-readable format (Article 16(4) of Directive (EU) 2019/770).

8.3 Renewals

An automatic renewal continues the existing contract and is not a new contract; it does not create a new statutory right of withdrawal. The Client may cancel at any time before renewal (Section 9). If the Client forgets to cancel a yearly subscription and requests a refund within 7 days after renewal without having used the Service in the new period (no Edit submitted), the Provider will refund the renewal payment as a goodwill gesture.

9. Cancellation by the Client

9.1 The Client may cancel the subscription at any time in the App (Account → Manage subscription → Cancel), as easily as it was ordered, or by e-mail to the address in Section 2. We confirm the cancellation by e-mail.

9.2 Cancellation takes effect at the end of the paid period. Until then the Website stays online and the Client can submit Edits. Payments for the unused part of a paid period are not refunded, except under Section 8, Section 18 (lack of conformity) and Section 15.5 (material change of the Service).

9.3 Deleting the account in the App also cancels the subscription and ends the Service (Section 17.4). The App warns the Client before confirmation.

10. Failed payment and suspension

10.1 If a renewal payment fails, Lemon Squeezy retries it and the Provider notifies the Client by e-mail and in the App.

10.2 If the payment is not made within 7 days of the first failed attempt, the Provider may suspend the Website (an information page is shown instead) and pause Edits. After payment the Website is restored without undue delay, usually automatically.

10.3 If payment is not made within 60 days of suspension, the contract ends. At least 14 days before deleting the Website we send the Client a notice and the option to download the Client Content (Section 17).

11. Edits and fair use

11.1 The Client submits Edits in the App (Requests → New request). The request is handled by an AI worker and checked by a human before publication (Section 12). The Client can see the status in the App.

11.2 An Edit is one request to change the existing Website within one subpage or one shared element, for example: changing or adding text, replacing or adding images, changing contact details, opening hours or prices, adding a section from existing blocks, changing a menu item, adding a blog post from the Client's text. Several changes in one request affecting different subpages count as several Edits; the Provider shows the Client how many Edits will be counted before processing.

11.3 The following are not Edits (and may be charged only with the Client's consent at a price communicated in advance): a new Website design, a new subpage beyond the Plan, a new feature (e.g. online shop, integration with an external system), translation of the whole Website, a larger content package, repair of errors caused by the Client's own intervention in the Website (Section 13.6).

11.4 The number of Edits resets at the start of each billing month (for yearly subscriptions, every month from the subscription start date). Unused Edits do not roll over. Edits beyond the Plan limit may be ordered separately at the price shown in the App before confirmation (from €10 excl. VAT), or the Client may upgrade.

11.5 Fair use (Business+). In the Business+ Plan the number of minor Edits is not capped by a number. A minor Edit is an Edit under Section 11.2. Fair use means use corresponding to the normal operation of a website of one business of the Client. In particular, the following is not fair use: submitting Edits for other websites or other persons, automated or bulk submission of requests, repeatedly switching and reverting the same changes without apparent reason, or splitting a larger change under Section 11.3 into minor Edits. If the Provider detects unfair use, it will first contact the Client and propose a solution (e.g. quote for the larger change). It may reasonably spread processing of further requests over time but may not refuse them without explanation.

11.6 Edits are made without undue delay in the order received. No processing time is guaranteed unless expressly stated in the App. Urgent repairs of a non-functioning Website (Section 15.3) take priority and do not count towards the limit.

12. Creating the Website, artificial intelligence and human review

12.1 AI transparency. The Provider uses artificial intelligence systems to create and edit the Website (e.g. to propose structure, texts and images and to process requests; in the App, the AI assistant "Aika" appears). AI outputs are reviewed by a human member of the Provider's team before publication. When communicating in the App, the Client always knows whether they are talking to AI or a human.

12.2 The Provider creates the Website based on the Client's questionnaire and materials and sends a preview for review before publication. Before publication the Client must check in particular the factual accuracy of the information (contact details, prices, description of services, legal information), as AI may produce inaccurate or unsuitable text. The Client is responsible for the factual accuracy of information about its business that it has approved.

12.3 AI visuals with people: if the Client supplies photographs of people and asks for them to be used in AI visuals, the Client confirms that it has the consent of the persons depicted. Images in which AI creates or alters the likeness of real people will be labelled on the Website as AI-generated or AI-edited, unless the depiction is evidently artistic or fictional (Article 50(4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 – AI Act).

12.4 Client cooperation: the Client provides the materials needed for the Website (questionnaire, logo, photographs, contact details) and answers the Provider's questions. If the Client does not provide materials, the Provider may complete the Website from available information using neutral texts and illustrative images; delays caused by missing materials are not the Provider's responsibility.

12.5 The design and technical solution (template, layout, tools used) are determined by the Provider taking the Client's wishes into account.

13. Client Content, responsibility and prohibited content

13.1 The Client is responsible for the Client Content and for Website content it has approved or supplied. The Client declares that it holds the necessary rights to the Client Content (copyright, photo licences, consent of persons depicted, right to use trade marks and names) and that publishing it does not infringe third-party rights or the law.

13.2 As operator of the Website, the Client is responsible for complying with legal obligations applicable to its business and website, in particular its own terms, privacy information for visitors, cookie consent and mandatory trader information. The Provider technically deploys a cookie banner and template texts it has available; this is not legal advice.

13.3 Prohibited content and use. The Website and the Service must not be used for: illegal content; infringement of intellectual property; fraud, phishing and misleading advertising; distribution of malware; spam; child sexual abuse material; incitement to violence or hatred; sale of illegal goods or services; adult content; unlicensed gambling; misuse of personal data; circumventing technical limits of the Service or attacking the Provider's infrastructure.

13.4 Reporting illegal content. Anyone may report content on the Website that they consider illegal by e-mail to nikol@netovapomoc.sk, stating the URL, the reason, their name and e-mail and a statement of good faith (Article 16 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 – Digital Services Act). The Provider will assess the notice without undue delay, objectively and impartially, and inform both the notifier and the Client of the outcome.

13.5 If the Provider restricts or removes content, it will inform the Client of the reasons (Article 17 DSA) and how to object via the contact e-mail. For manifestly illegal content or security threats the Provider may disable content or the Website immediately; otherwise it will first ask the Client to remedy within a reasonable time.

13.6 Client interventions. If the Provider gives the Client limited access to the Website administration, the Client uses it only to edit content. To establish the cause of any error, the Website logs administrative changes (who, when, what, IP address). The Provider may charge a service fee (from €10 excl. VAT) for repairing an error demonstrably caused by the Client's intervention, only with the price communicated in advance; in case of doubt it decides in the Client's favour.

14. Intellectual property, domain and e-mail

14.1 Client Content remains the Client's. The Client grants the Provider a free, non-exclusive licence to use the Client Content to the extent necessary to provide the Service (processing, editing, placing on the Website, backups) for the term of the contract and subsequent retention under Section 17.

14.2 Texts and images created for the Website (including AI outputs) may be freely used by the Client for any purpose during and after the contract; the Provider claims no rights in them. However, the Provider does not guarantee that AI outputs are protected by copyright or unique. Stock images are subject to the licence terms of the stock library.

14.3 The technical solution of the Website (source code, template, database structure, plugin configuration, design components and the Provider's tools) remains with the Provider or its licensors. The Client receives a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the Website within the Service for the term of the subscription. Server access (FTP, SSH, database) and transfer of a functioning Website to another provider are not part of the Service; the Provider may, on request, offer a transfer of the Website at a price agreed in advance.

14.4 Domain. A domain owned by the Client remains the Client's; the Provider only configures its routing. If the Provider registers a domain for the Client under the Business or Business+ Plan, it will register it in the Client's name as registrant (where the registry allows) and after the contract ends will transfer it or provide the authorisation code free of charge on request; the Client pays only any registry fees for further periods. The Provider will never withhold a domain as security.

14.5 Mailboxes included in the Plan are part of the Service. When the contract ends or on downgrade, the Provider will cancel them after the notice under Section 17; until then the Client may download or forward its mail.

14.6 The Provider may place a discreet "Website: Netová pomoc" link in the Website footer; Business+ Clients may ask for it to be removed.

15. Operation, backups, availability and changes to the Service

15.1 The Provider operates the Website with professional care, provides software updates, an SSL certificate and appropriate technical and organisational security measures.

15.2 Backups of the Website are normally made daily. Backups serve to restore operation in case of failure; they are not an archive for the Client, and the Client is not entitled to a specific older version where this is technically impossible.

15.3 Availability. The Provider makes reasonable efforts to keep the Website available at all times; availability is checked by automatic monitoring. The Provider does not guarantee any specific availability percentage (SLA) and is not liable for outages caused by scheduled maintenance (announced in advance where possible), force majeure, third-party attacks, failures of infrastructure providers, domain registries, DNS or the Client's connection. Outages constituting a lack of conformity are fixed without undue delay and the Client has the rights under Section 18.

15.4 Updates. The Provider supplies the updates necessary to keep the Service in conformity, including security updates (Article 8(2) of Directive (EU) 2019/770), and informs the Client in the App where they affect the Client.

15.5 Changes to the Service. The Provider may change the Service for valid reasons: changes in law, security, change of technology or supplier, improvements, discontinuation of a third-party tool. A change must not cause additional costs to the Client. If a change negatively affects the Client's access to or use of the Service in more than a minor way, the Provider will notify it on a durable medium (e-mail) at least 30 days in advance, and the Client may terminate the contract free of charge within 30 days of the notice or the change (whichever is later); the Provider will refund the pro-rated price for the unused period (Article 19 of Directive (EU) 2019/770).

15.6 The Provider may use subcontractors (e.g. hosting, AI tools, automation tools). It is responsible for their performance as for its own.

16. Termination by the Provider

16.1 The Provider may terminate the contract without giving reasons with 60 days' notice to the end of a subscription period; it will refund the pro-rated price for any period after termination.

16.2 The Provider may terminate or suspend the Service with immediate effect if the Client materially breaches these Terms, in particular Section 13.3 (prohibited content), repeatedly breaches Section 11.5 despite a warning, or if required by a public authority decision. For less serious breaches the Provider first asks the Client to remedy within at least 7 days.

16.3 If the Provider ends the Service without breach by the Client, it will let the Client download the Client Content and transfer the domain under Section 17.

16.4 If the Provider discontinues MintyRobot as a whole, it will notify Clients at least 90 days in advance, refund the pro-rated subscription and help with the transition (export of Client Content, domain transfer).

17. What happens to the Website and data after the contract ends

17.1 After the contract ends (cancellation, expiry without renewal, withdrawal or termination under Section 10.3) the Provider switches off the Website.

17.2 Export of Client Content. Within 30 days of the end of the contract the Client may request, in the App or by e-mail, a free export of the Client Content: Website texts, images and photographs, logo, data submitted via Website forms and questionnaire answers, in commonly used formats (e.g. DOCX/TXT, JPG/PNG, CSV). Export of a functioning Website (code, database) is not part of the Service (Section 14.3).

17.3 After 30 days from the end of the contract the Provider deletes the Website and the Client Content; they are deleted from backups in the normal rotation cycle. Data the Provider must or may retain longer (e.g. records of the contract and consents until limitation periods expire) are governed by the Privacy Notice.

17.4 Deleting the account in the App is a request to end the Service and delete data. If the Client deletes the account during a paid period, the subscription is cancelled and the Website is switched off at the moment of deletion; payments for the unused period are not refunded except under Section 8. Before deletion the App offers an export of the Client Content.

18. Lack of conformity and complaints

18.1 The Provider is responsible for the Service having, throughout its provision, the characteristics agreed in the contract and those that can reasonably be expected of such a service (for Consumers, Articles 7, 8 and 11–14 of Directive (EU) 2019/770 as transposed in Sections 852d–852m of the Slovak Civil Code, and the applicable law of the Consumer's residence).

18.2 The Client submits a complaint in the App (Requests or Account → Help) or by e-mail to the address in Section 2, describing the defect. The Provider promptly confirms receipt and states the time limit for remedying the defect, which will not exceed 30 days from the complaint unless a longer period is justified by an objective reason beyond the Provider's control.

18.3 The Provider remedies the defect free of charge. If it cannot be remedied, is not remedied in time, recurs or is serious, the Consumer is entitled to a proportionate price reduction for the time the Service was not in conformity or, for a defect that is not minor, to terminate the contract. Reductions or refunds are paid within 14 days.

18.4 If the Provider rejects a complaint, it will give reasons in writing (e-mail).

18.5 The following are not defects: errors caused by the Client Content or the Client's intervention, incompatibility of the Client's device with commonly supported browsers, or limitations expressly stated in these Terms (e.g. Section 15.3).

18.6 For Businesses, claims for defects are governed by the Slovak Commercial Code; a Business must notify a defect without undue delay after discovering it.

19. Liability for damage

19.1 The Provider is liable for damage caused by breach of its obligations in accordance with the law.

19.2 Towards Consumers, the Provider's liability is not limited beyond what the law allows.

19.3 Towards Businesses, the parties declare in accordance with Section 379 of the Slovak Commercial Code that, at the time the contract is concluded, the Provider foresees as possible damage from a breach of its obligations at most an amount equal to the price the Client paid for the Service in the 12 months before the damage occurred. In particular, the Provider does not foresee and is not liable for lost profit due to Website outages, loss of business, reputational harm or damage caused by Client Content. This does not apply to damage caused intentionally or by gross negligence or to personal injury.

19.4 The Provider is not liable for third-party services the Client connects to the Website at its own request (e.g. its own analytics, advertising pixels, external booking systems) or for decisions of search engines and social networks (rankings, display).

20. Personal data

20.1 Processing of the Client's personal data as a user of the App and the Service is governed by the MintyRobot App Privacy Notice and the Provider's general Privacy Policy at netovapomoc.sk.

20.2 Personal data of Website visitors. When operating the Website (hosting, forms, business mailboxes, traffic measurement, admin change log), the Provider processes personal data of the Client's visitors and customers as a processor on behalf of the Client, who is the controller. This processing is governed by Annex 2 – Data Processing Agreement (Article 28 GDPR), which forms part of the contract.

21. The MintyRobot App

21.1 The Provider grants the Client a non-exclusive, non-transferable, free right to use the App on devices it owns or controls, solely to manage the Service while the account exists.

21.2 The Client must not reverse engineer, copy, modify or use the App for any other purpose except as permitted by law.

21.3 Sign-in uses a one-time code sent to the Client's e-mail. The Client is responsible for securing its mailbox.

21.4 The Client may delete the account at any time directly in the App (Account → Delete account) or via the web link given in the app store listing; consequences are set out in Section 17.4 and the App Privacy Notice.

21.5 App features using AI (voice recording transcription, sorting answers, interface translation) are assistive. The Client always sees the result and can correct it before submitting.

21.6 Apple App Store addendum. If the Client downloaded the App from the Apple App Store, the following also applies:
a) These Terms are concluded between the Client and the Provider only, and not with Apple Inc. ("Apple"). The Provider, not Apple, is solely responsible for the App and its content.
b) The licence under Section 21.1 is limited to use of the App on Apple-branded products that the Client owns or controls, as permitted by the Usage Rules in the Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions (except that the App may be accessed by other accounts via Family Sharing or volume purchasing).
c) Apple has no obligation whatsoever to furnish any maintenance and support services for the App; these are provided by the Provider (contact in Section 2).
d) In the event of any failure of the App to conform to any applicable warranty, the Client may notify Apple, and Apple will refund the purchase price of the App (the App is free); to the maximum extent permitted by law, Apple has no other warranty obligation with respect to the App, and any other claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs or expenses attributable to any failure to conform are the Provider's responsibility.
e) The Provider, not Apple, is responsible for addressing any claims of the Client or any third party relating to the App or its possession and/or use, including product liability claims, claims that the App fails to conform to any legal or regulatory requirement, and claims arising under consumer protection, privacy or similar legislation.
f) In the event of any third-party claim that the App or its possession and use infringes that third party's intellectual property rights, the Provider, not Apple, is solely responsible for the investigation, defence, settlement and discharge of such claim.
g) The Client represents and warrants that it is not located in a country subject to a U.S. Government embargo or designated by the U.S. Government as a "terrorist supporting" country, and is not listed on any U.S. Government list of prohibited or restricted parties.
h) The Client must comply with applicable third-party terms of agreement when using the App (e.g. its mobile carrier).
i) Apple and Apple's subsidiaries are third-party beneficiaries of these Terms, and upon the Client's acceptance, Apple will have the right (and will be deemed to have accepted the right) to enforce these Terms against the Client as a third-party beneficiary.

21.7 Google Play. If the Client downloaded the App from Google Play, the Google Play Terms of Service also apply; Google is not responsible for the App.

22. Communication

22.1 Communication takes place in the App and by e-mail. Notices under these Terms (price change, change of Terms, notice before deletion) are sent to the Client's account e-mail and are thus delivered on a durable medium.

22.2 We always send service messages (Website status, outage, payment, security). We send offers of other services only as permitted by law, and the Client can opt out at any time.

23. Changes to these Terms

23.1 The Provider may change these Terms for the valid reasons in Section 23.2. It will notify the Client by e-mail and in the App at least 30 days before the change takes effect, explaining what changes.
